prs.title: Add draft ZIP: Lock-weighted Coinholder Polling
prs.author: arya2
prs.bodyExcerpt: Draft ZIP, Process category, Status: Draft. Proposes that coinholder polls weight each ballot by how long the voter's ZEC is locked past the snapshot, not only by how much ZEC they hold. Weight is linear in lock length up to a cap of one halving interval; unlocked coins keep a floor weight of one te

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,400 @@
+    ZIP: Unassigned
+    Title: Lock-weighted Coinholder Polling
+    Owners: Arya <arya@zfnd.org>
+    Status: Draft
+    Category: Process
+    Created: 2026-11-03
+    License: MIT
+    Discussions-To: <URL TBD>
+
+
+# Terminology
+
+The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", and "MAY" in this
+document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [^BCP14] when, and only
+when, they appear in all capitals.
+
+The terms "Mainnet" and "Testnet" in this document are to be interpreted as
+defined in the Zcash protocol specification [^protocol-networks].
+
+The term "*Ironwood pool*" is to be interpreted as described in ZIP 229
+[^zip-0229].
+
+The terms "Coinholder-Controlled Fund" and "Key-Holder Organizations" are to be
+interpreted as described in ZIP 1016 [^zip-1016]. The term "Deferred Dev Fund
+Lockbox" is to be interpreted as described in ZIP 1015 [^zip-1015].
+
+Poll
+
+: A vote in which each ballot carries a ZEC amount.
+
+Poll operator
+
+: Whoever announces a poll, verifies ballots, and publishes results.
+
+Snapshot height
+
+: The block height $S$ at which holdings are measured.
+
+Close height
+
+: The height $C$ of the last block in which a ballot can be accepted.
+
+Lock record
+
+: A triple $(v, u, c)$: a value $v$ in zatoshi, an unlock height $u$ at or
+  before which consensus forbids spending it ($u = 0$ if unlocked), and an
+  evidence class $c$. Its lock length is $\ell = \max(0, u - S)$ blocks.
+
+
+# Abstract
+
+Coinholder polls count one ZEC as one vote at a snapshot height, and coins may
+be moved right after the snapshot. This ZIP changes only the weighting: a
+ballot's weight rises linearly with how long its coins stay locked past the
+snapshot, up to a cap of one halving interval; unlocked coins keep a small
+floor weight. One evidence class works today: transparent outputs locked
+with `OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY`. A second class for shielded locks is reserved
+for a consensus ZIP. Quorum and the ZIP 1016 participation threshold stay in
+unweighted ZEC. The transparent class reveals the voter's output, amount, and
+unlock height on chain, which the current shielded polling path does not; the
+shielded class is the intended end state.
+
+
+# Motivation
+
+Coinholder polling gives holders a voice alongside developers, users, and
+miners. ZIP 1016 [^zip-1016] makes it the deciding input for the
+Coinholder-Controlled Fund, and about 2.4 million of 3.6 million eligible ZEC
+voted in the NU7 scope poll of September 2026 [^coindesk-nu7].
+
+The status quo is one ZEC, one vote, at a snapshot, with coins movable the
+moment the snapshot passes [^forum-nu7-vote]. Someone who buys the week of
+the vote and sells the week after is not a holder; they are renting a vote.
+This ZIP favours people credibly in it for the long haul. Someone willing to
+lock ZEC for years should have a big say, not the only say. A whale who locks
+for years still gets a big vote; they have put their coins where their vote
+is. The change removes the cheap vote, not the big one.
+
+## Scope decision
+
+There is no timelock for shielded notes. Transparent outputs can be locked
+with `OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY` [^bip-0065], which Zebra enforces on every
+transparent input [^zebra-script] `[VERIFY: enforced by zcashd since
+genesis]`. Sapling, Orchard, and Ironwood notes have no script and no lock
+field, and a transaction's `lock_time` is ignored when no transparent input
+has a non-final sequence number [^zebra-locktime], so it cannot lock a
+shielded-only spend. Three options were considered:
+
+1. A process-only ZIP using transparent locks. It works at the protocol
+   level, not the tooling level: the live mechanism accepts only notes in the
+   *Ironwood pool* [^zcashlabs-voting]. It asks holders to unshield for full
+   weight, which is at odds with the point of Zcash. Not acceptable as the
+   only option.
+2. A consensus ZIP adding a lock to shielded notes. The smallest version is a
+   lock-height field in the Ironwood note commitment, one circuit constraint,
+   and one consensus rule (see [Class S]). That is a new circuit version for a
+   pool created, with formal verification, after the Orchard soundness
+   vulnerability [^zip-0229]. It is not small and needs a network upgrade.
+3. Two ZIPs: this process ZIP, defining weighting over any lock the protocol
+   can prove, with the transparent class as an interim, plus a later consensus
+   ZIP for shielded locks.
+
+Option 3 is chosen. Everything below is defined over lock records, so the
+shielded class can be added without rewriting this ZIP.
+
+
+# Privacy Implications
+
+Under the live mechanism, validators learn neither who voted nor how much ZEC
+a ballot carried; amounts are encrypted and only totals are decrypted
+[^zcashlabs-voting]. A ballot under [Class T] reveals an output, its value,
+and its unlock height on chain to everyone, and links the ballot to that
+output unless the operator encrypts ballot contents. A voter who unshields to
+lock also reveals the unshielding transaction. That cost is why Class S is the
+intended end state.
+
+The shielded class is required to reveal no more than the current shielded
+path: the lock length stays a private witness, the multiplier is applied
+inside the proof, and locked notes are indistinguishable from unlocked notes
+on chain, including when spent.
+
+
+# Requirements
+
+* A ballot's weight depends on both the amount of ZEC and how long it is
+  locked past the snapshot.
+* Borrowing, hedging, or splitting to gain weight costs more than under
+  amount-only weighting.
+* Weighting is defined over an abstract lock record, so shielded locks can be
+  added without changing the rules.
+* The shielded class reveals no more than the current shielded polling path.
+* Coins with no holder, such as protocol-level lockboxes, cannot be voted.
+
+
+# Non-requirements
+
+* This ZIP does not change who is eligible to vote, what polls are held, or
+  what polls decide. It changes weighting only.
+* It does not propose on-chain binding governance. Polls remain what ZIP 1016
+  says they are.
+* It does not change mining, block subsidy, or funding streams.
+* It does not verify custody.
+
+
+# Specification
+
+## Parameters
+
+$S$ and $C$ are chosen by the poll operator per poll. The floor is
+$f = 1/10$. The cap $L$ is the halving interval in effect at height $S$:
+$\mathsf{PostBlossomHalvingInterval} = 1{,}680{,}000$ blocks before NU7
+activation and $\mathsf{PostNU7HalvingInterval} = 5{,}040{,}000$ blocks from
+NU7 activation [^zip-0218]. Both are about four years.
+
+## Weight function
+
+For a lock record $(v, u, c)$ with lock length $\ell = \max(0, u - S)$:
+
+$$m(\ell) = f + (1 - f) \cdot \frac{\min(\ell, L)}{L}, \qquad w = v \cdot m(\ell)$$
+
+If $u \leq C$, the record MUST be counted as unlocked ($\ell = 0$). A ballot's
+weight is the sum of $w$ over its lock records.
+
+| $\ell / L$ | $m(\ell)$ | at the four-year cap |
+|-----------:|----------:|----------------------|
+| 0          | 0.100     | unlocked             |
+| 1/16       | 0.156     | 3 months             |
+| 1/8        | 0.213     | 6 months             |
+| 1/4        | 0.325     | 1 year               |
+| 1/2        | 0.550     | 2 years              |
+| 1 or more  | 1.000     | 4 years or more      |
+
+## Lock records
+
+An operator MUST accept Class H and at least one lock class, and MUST reject
+any ballot whose evidence fails verification; a failed record MUST NOT be
+counted under Class H.
+
+### Class H
+
+Class H evidence is whatever proof of holding at $S$ the operator already
+accepts, such as a proof of unspent Ironwood notes. It yields $(v, 0,
+\mathrm{H})$ and counts at the floor.
+
+### Class T
+
+Class T evidence is a transparent output whose `scriptPubKey` is a
+pay-to-script-hash of the redeem script
+
+    <u> OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY OP_DROP <pubkey> OP_CHECKSIG
+
+where `<u>` is a minimally encoded script number with
+$1 \leq u < 500{,}000{,}000$ (a block height, not a Unix time) [^bip-0065].
+The ballot carries the outpoint, the redeem script, and an ECDSA signature
+over secp256k1 by `pubkey`, as for `OP_CHECKSIG`, over a message $M$ defined
+by the operator. $M$ MUST include a poll identifier and MUST bind the ballot
+contents or a commitment to them.
+
+The operator MUST check that:
+
+1. the output exists and is unspent in the chain state at height $S$;
+2. the `scriptPubKey` equals the P2SH encoding of the supplied redeem script;
+3. the redeem script matches the template and $u$ is in height form;
+4. the signature is valid for `pubkey` over $M$;
+5. the outpoint has not been used in another ballot of this poll.
+
+The lock record is $(v, u, \mathrm{T})$ with $v$ the output's value.
+Operators MAY also accept an `OP_CHECKMULTISIG` variant of the template with
+$m$ valid signatures.
+
+### Class S
+
+Class S, shielded locks, is reserved for a consensus ZIP. That ZIP MUST
+provide: a way to fix an unlock height at note creation that consensus
+enforces on spends; a proof usable within the operator's shielded path that
+yields a lock record for notes unspent at $S$, with the multiplier applied
+inside the proof; and locked notes indistinguishable from unlocked notes on
+chain, including when spent.
+
+The smallest design known: a lock-height field inside the
+Ironwood note commitment (zero for none); a circuit constraint that the field
+is at most a per-bundle minimum height; a consensus rule that a transaction
+with a non-zero minimum height is invalid in any block below it; and wallets
+that set that value on every transaction so locked spends do not stand out.
+`[VERIFY: fit with ZIP 229 and the Ironwood circuit]`
+
+## Counting
+
+For each option the operator MUST compute the weighted total $W$, the sum of
+ballot weights, and the unweighted total $V$, the sum of $v$ over the same
+ballots. The outcome among options MUST be decided on $W$. Any quorum, and the
+420,000 ZEC participation threshold of ZIP 1016 [^zip-1016], MUST be measured
+on $V$.
+
+## Excluded coins
+
+Value in the Deferred Dev Fund Lockbox [^zip-2001] and the NSM value balance
+[^zip-0237] are chain value pool balances, not outputs or notes. They cannot
+produce lock records and MUST NOT be counted.
+
+## Poll operator obligations
+
+Before height $S$ the operator MUST publish $S$, $C$, $L$, $f$, the accepted
+evidence classes, and the format of $M$. The operator SHOULD NOT verify
+Class T evidence until the block at height $S$ has at least 100
+confirmations. After the poll the operator MUST publish $W$ and $V$ for every
+option and SHOULD publish only totals. Operators MAY rehearse on Testnet,
+where Mainnet thresholds do not apply.
+
+
+# Security Considerations
+
+**Borrow-to-vote.** Borrow ZEC, lock it, vote, repay after unlock. At an
+annual borrowing cost $r$, a one-week unlocked borrow costs about $r/52$ of
+$v$ for weight $0.1\,v$; a lock of $L$ costs about $4r$ of $v$ for weight $v$,
+roughly twenty times more per unit of weight, and the loan must run until
+$u$.
+
+**Lock-and-hedge.** Lock $v$ and short $v$ elsewhere, voting with no net
+exposure. This costs funding and margin over $\ell$ and remains possible; the
+design raises cost, it does not make this impossible.
+
+**Splitting.** Because $m$ is linear below the cap, weight per ZEC-block is
+constant, so no partition of a holding across lock lengths changes its total
+weight.
+
+**Last-minute locks.** A lock placed the day before $S$ that reaches past $L$
+counts in full. The forward commitment is the same whenever the lock was
+placed; what such a voter lacks is past holding, which this ZIP does not
+weigh. See [Open questions].
+
+**Vote buying** is unchanged in kind. A seller must lock to sell full weight,
+so the price rises, but the trade exists.
+
+**Custodians.** A custodian that owes coins on demand cannot lock them without
+a liquidity mismatch, so voting customer coins at full weight gets harder.
+That is intended. The limits: a custodian can lock its own float or accept
+the mismatch, and this ZIP does not verify custody.
+
+
+# Rationale
+
+## Alternatives considered
+
+*Amount only (status quo).* One ZEC, one vote, movable right after the
+snapshot [^forum-nu7-vote]. The vote can be rented for a week's exposure.
+
+*One person, one vote.* Zcash has no sybil-resistant identity. The Zcash
+Community Advisory Panel already gives a per-person signal alongside
+coinholder polls [^zfnd-nu7-results].
+
+*Square root or logarithm of amount.* Without identity, any concave function
+of amount is defeated by splitting a holding across ballots.
+
+*Conviction tiers* [^polkadot-opengov]. Multipliers that step with lock
+length let a holder pick the best point on the curve by splitting. Linear with
+a cap, as in Curve's vote-escrow [^curve-vecrv], does not.
+
+*Age weighting.* Weight by how long coins have already been held. For
+shielded notes this is provable today without a consensus change: the note
+commitment tree is append-only, so a note's position bounds its creation
+height, and the proof-of-balance draft [^draft-str4d-balance-proof] already
+proves holding at a snapshot. In the *Ironwood pool*, age is bounded by the
+pool's activation in July 2026 [^zip-0258] and reset by migration
+[^zip-0318]. It is backward-looking, so it does not express willingness to
+stay, but it defeats buy-vote-sell and last-minute locks directly. Not
+adopted here; see [Open questions].
+
+*Time-averaged balance.* Several snapshots, several proofs per ballot, still
+passive. A forward lock supplies its own window.
+
+## Rationale for the cap and floor
+
+The cap is one halving interval: the longest horizon over which the protocol
+itself plans issuance, and the four-year maximum of vote-escrow systems
+[^curve-vecrv]. The floor is non-zero so that this ZIP does not change who
+can vote; zero would exclude every shielded holder until Class S exists. One
+tenth is the weight of an unlocked vote in Polkadot's conviction voting
+[^polkadot-opengov].
+
+## Rationale for measuring in blocks
+
+`OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY` heights are blocks, and NU7 cuts the target spacing
+from 75 to 25 seconds [^zip-0218], so a lock expressed in time would change
+meaning at activation. Measuring $\ell$ and $L$ in blocks at height $S$ keeps
+the weight well defined.
+
+
+# Open questions
+
+* Will any poll operator add a Class T path to a shielded-only mechanism, and
+  what is $M$ there?
+* Should past holding (age) count toward $\ell$, generally or as the shielded
+  interim before Class S?
+* Are $f = 1/10$ and $L$ = one halving interval right? Should $f$ drop to
+  zero once Class S exists?
+* Should a lock have to reach past a fixed horizon rather than only past $C$?
+* Should Coinholder-Controlled Fund coins held by the Key-Holder
+  Organizations [^zip-0271] be excluded? ZIP 1016 restricts no one.
+* Should Class T accept time-form or `OP_CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY` locks
+  (ZIP 112 [^zip-0112])?
+* ZIP 1016 decides on ZEC cast in favour and, between competing grants, on
+  ZEC committed in support. Deciding on $W$ changes that; applying this ZIP
+  to ZIP 1016 votes needs its Owners and an Updates header.
+* Which network upgrade could carry Class S? `[VERIFY: NU8 planning]`
+
+
+# Deployment
+
+This ZIP applies to a poll when the operator announces, before $S$, that the
+poll follows it. Class T is usable once an operator implements its
+verification. Class S is usable only after its consensus ZIP activates on
+Mainnet; until then, shielded coins vote under Class H at the floor weight.
+
+

@@ -0,0 +1,279 @@
+    ZIP: Unassigned
+    Title: 10-second Block Target Spacing
+    Owners: Marek <marek@zfnd.org>
+    Status: Draft
+    Category: Consensus
+    Created: 2026-10-31
+    License: MIT
+
+
+# Terminology
+
+The key words "MUST", "SHALL", "SHOULD", and "SHOULD NOT" in this document are
+to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [^BCP14] when, and only when, they
+appear in all capitals.
+
+The term "network upgrade" is to be interpreted as defined in ZIP 200.
+[^zip-0200]
+
+The term "block target spacing" is to be interpreted as defined in ZIP 218.
+[^zip-0218]
+
+The character § is used when referring to sections of the Zcash Protocol
+Specification. [^protocol]
+
+The terms "Mainnet" and "Testnet" are to be interpreted as described in
+§ 3.12 'Mainnet and Testnet'. [^protocol-networks]
+
+"NU8" is the code name of the network upgrade that deploys this proposal.
+
+
+# Abstract
+
+This proposal changes the block target spacing from 25 seconds to 10 seconds
+in NU8. The block subsidy, the block size limit, and the shielded action limits
+of each block are scaled by the same factor, so that issuance, block space, and
+shielded capacity per unit of time are unchanged.
+
+
+# Motivation
+
+ZIP 218 reduces the block target spacing from 75 seconds to 25 seconds in NU7
+in order to reduce transaction latency. [^zip-0218] This proposal reduces it to
+10 seconds, which reduces the expected time to a first confirmation from 25
+seconds to 10 seconds.
+
+The proposal changes latency only. Each quantity that NU7 specifies per unit of
+time is preserved: issuance, funding stream address periods, reissuance by the
+Network Sustainability Mechanism, the duration of the difficulty averaging
+window, and the resource limits of the block chain.
+
+
+# Specification
+
+The changes below are made to the Zcash Protocol Specification [^protocol] and
+to ZIPs 207, 214, and 237 [^zip-0207] [^zip-0214] [^zip-0237], as amended for
+NU7 by ZIP 218 [^zip-0218] and ZIP 259 [^zip-0259].
+
+## Block target spacing
+
+In § 5.3 'Constants' [^protocol-constants], define:
+
+$$\mathsf{NU8ActivationHeight} : \mathbb{N}$$
+$$\mathsf{PostNU8PoWTargetSpacing} : \mathbb{N} := 10 \textsf{ seconds}$$
+
+In § 7.7.3 'Difficulty adjustment' [^protocol-diffadjustment], define:
+
+$$\mathsf{NU8PoWTargetSpacingRatio} : \mathbb{Q} := \mathsf{PostNU7PoWTargetSpacing} \;/\; \mathsf{PostNU8PoWTargetSpacing} = 5/2$$
+
+$$\mathsf{IsNU8Activated} : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathsf{false}, \mathsf{true}\}$$
+$$\mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height}) := (\mathsf{height} \geq \mathsf{NU8ActivationHeight})$$
+
+On each network, $\mathsf{NU8ActivationHeight}$ SHALL be even.
+
+In the definition of $\mathsf{PoWTargetSpacing}$ in ZIP 218, replace the case
+"otherwise" with "if $\mathsf{IsNU7Activated}(\mathsf{height})$ and not
+$\mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height})$", and add the case
+$\mathsf{PostNU8PoWTargetSpacing}$ "otherwise".
+
+## Difficulty averaging window
+
+In § 5.3 'Constants', define:
+
+$$\mathsf{PostNU8PoWAveragingWindow} : \mathbb{N} := 255$$
+
+In the definition of $\mathsf{PoWAveragingWindow}$ in ZIP 218, replace the case
+"otherwise" with "if $\mathsf{IsNU7Activated}(\mathsf{height})$ and not
+$\mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height})$", and add the case
+$\mathsf{PostNU8PoWAveragingWindow}$ "otherwise".
+
+The averaging window timespan therefore remains 2,550 seconds.
+
+## Halving interval and block subsidy
+
+Define:
+
+$$\mathsf{PostNU8HalvingInterval} : \mathbb{N} := \mathsf{PostNU7HalvingInterval} \cdot \mathsf{NU8PoWTargetSpacingRatio} = 12{,}600{,}000$$
+
+In the definition of $\mathsf{Halving}$ in ZIP 218, replace the case
+"otherwise" with "if $\mathsf{IsNU7Activated}(\mathsf{height})$ and not
+$\mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height})$", and add the case:
+
+$$
+\left\lfloor \dfrac{\mathsf{BlossomActivationHeight} - \mathsf{SlowStartShift}}{\mathsf{PreBlossomHalvingInterval}}
+  + \dfrac{\mathsf{NU7ActivationHeight} - \mathsf{BlossomActivationHeight}}{\mathsf{PostBlossomHalvingInterval}}
+  + \dfrac{\mathsf{NU8ActivationHeight} - \mathsf{NU7ActivationHeight}}{\mathsf{PostNU7HalvingInterval}}
+  + \dfrac{\mathsf{height} - \mathsf{NU8ActivationHeight}}{\mathsf{PostNU8HalvingInterval}} \right\rfloor,
+  \quad \textsf{otherwise}
+$$
+
+In the definition of $\mathsf{ScheduledBlockSubsidy}$ in ZIP 237, replace the
+condition "if $\mathsf{IsNU7Activated}(\mathsf{height})$" of the case added by
+ZIP 218 with "if $\mathsf{IsNU7Activated}(\mathsf{height})$ and not
+$\mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height})$", and add the case:
+
+$$
+\mathsf{floor}\left(\dfrac{\mathsf{MaxBlockSubsidy}}{\mathsf{BlossomPoWTargetSpacingRatio} \cdot \mathsf{NU7PoWTargetSpacingRatio} \cdot \mathsf{NU8PoWTargetSpacingRatio} \cdot 2^{\mathsf{Halving}(\mathsf{height})}}\right),
+  \quad \textsf{if } \mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height})
+$$
+
+The denominator is $15 \cdot 2^{\mathsf{Halving}(\mathsf{height})}$.
+
+## Block size and shielded action limits
+
+For a block at a height for which $\mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height})$,
+the size of the block MUST be less than or equal to 800,000 bytes, in place of
+the limit of 2,000,000 bytes in § 7.6 'Block Header Encoding and Consensus'.
+[^protocol-blockheader]
+
+For such a block, the shielded action limits of ZIP 218 apply with
+$\mathsf{GlobalShieldedBudget} = 132$,
+$\mathsf{OrchardProtocolBlockActionLimit} = 132$, and
+$\mathsf{SaplingBlockIOLimit} = 120$. $\mathsf{SproutBlockJoinSplitLimit}$
+remains 0.
+
+## Funding streams
+
+Let $A$, $R$, $C$, $I$, and $H_1$ be as in the definition of
+$\mathsf{AddressPeriod}$ in Revision 2 of ZIP 207, and let
+$B = \mathsf{NU8ActivationHeight}$. In that definition, replace the case
+"otherwise" with "if $\mathsf{IsNU7Activated}(\mathsf{height})$ and not
+$\mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height})$", and add the case:
+
+$$
+\mathsf{floor}\left(\dfrac{5\left(R(A + I - H_1) + B - A\right) + 2(\mathsf{height} - B)}{5RC}\right),
+  \quad \textsf{otherwise}
+$$
+
+This preserves the address index at NU8 activation. Each later address period
+lasts $5RC/2 = 262{,}500$ blocks.
+
+For each funding stream that is active at $B$ and whose end height is
+$\mathsf{HeightForHalving}(3)$ by Revision 3 of ZIP 214, the end height SHALL
+be $\mathsf{HeightForHalving}(3)$ calculated using the $\mathsf{Halving}$
+function of this proposal. If $H_3$ is the third-halving height under ZIP 218
+(6,132,390 on Mainnet and 4,497,948 on Testnet), this end height is
+$B + 5(H_3 - B)/2$. The number of addresses that ZIP 207 requires
+for each such stream is unchanged.
+
+## Network Sustainability Mechanism
+
+In ZIP 237, $\mathsf{HalvingInterval}(\mathsf{height})$ is
+$\mathsf{PostNU8HalvingInterval}$ if $\mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height})$.
+From NU8 activation, $\mathsf{BLOCK\_SUBSIDY\_FRACTION}$ is therefore
+$550 / 10^{10}$.
+
+If $B$ is less than the $\mathsf{DEPLOYMENT\_BLOCK\_HEIGHT}$ that ZIP 237
+specifies for a network, then $\mathsf{DEPLOYMENT\_BLOCK\_HEIGHT}$ for that
+network SHALL instead be calculated as in ZIP 237, with $B$ in place of $A$,
+with $\mathsf{ScheduledBlockSubsidy}$, $H_3$, and $H_4$ as specified by this
+proposal, and with 550 in place of 1375. NU8 activation heights SHALL be chosen
+so that this height exists before $H_4$. The NU8 deployment ZIP specifies the
+resulting height for each network.
+
+## Minimum-difficulty blocks on Testnet
+
+On Testnet, from NU8 activation, the minimum-difficulty threshold specified by
+ZIP 218 is $45 \cdot \mathsf{PoWTargetSpacing}(\mathsf{height})$ seconds, which
+remains 450 seconds.
+
+## Unchanged consensus rules
+
+Consensus rules that are expressed in blocks and not changed above, including
+the coinbase maturity of 100 blocks and $\mathsf{PoWMedianBlockSpan}$, are
+unchanged.
+
+## Non-consensus changes
+
+From NU8 activation:
+
+- Wallets SHOULD use a default expiry delta of 300 blocks, in place of the 120
+  blocks recommended by ZIP 218.
+- Nodes SHOULD support rolling back at least 1,500 blocks, in place of the 600
+  blocks recommended by ZIP 218.
+- Implementations SHOULD multiply the block-count constants that ZIP 218
+  multiplies by 3 by $\mathsf{NU8PoWTargetSpacingRatio}$, rounding up.
+- Nodes SHOULD NOT admit to their mempools or relay, and wallets SHOULD NOT
+  create, a transaction that alone exceeds the block size or shielded action
+  limits above.
+
+
+# Rationale
+
+A target spacing of 10 seconds makes each scaled quantity an integer: the
+averaging window of 255 blocks, the halving interval of 12,600,000 blocks, the
+address period of 262,500 blocks, and the limits of 800,000 bytes, 132
+actions, and 120 Sapling inputs and outputs.
+
+Every post-NU7 halving height is even on both networks. An even activation
+height $B$ therefore maps each such height $H$ to the integer height
+$B + 5(H - B)/2$, so that no halving boundary falls within a 25-second block.
+
+Scaling the per-block limits by 2/5 keeps the worst-case validation work,
+compact sync bandwidth, and chain growth per unit of time at their NU7 values.
+ZIP 218 bounds worst-case compact sync bandwidth at 169.10 MB per day.
+[^zip-0218] Without the scaling, each of these would increase by a factor of
+5/2.
+
+The post-NU8 block subsidy differs from 2/5 of the post-NU7 block subsidy by
+less than one zatoshi, due to rounding. If NU8 activates before the third
+halving, this reduces total scheduled issuance, relative to ZIP 218, by
+$(H_3 - B)/2$ zatoshi before the third halving and by 1.134 ZEC after it.
+
+
+# Security and Privacy Considerations
+
+The stale block rate increases with the ratio of block propagation time to the
+block target spacing. ZIP 218 reports a stale block rate of 4.86% for 2 MB
+blocks at 25-second spacing on a 99-node devnet. [^zip-0218] The rate at
+10-second spacing has not been measured; it needs to be measured before
+deployment. Smaller blocks and compact block relay [^draft-compact-block-relay]
+reduce propagation time.
+
+A given number of confirmations corresponds to 2.5 times less time. Where
+propagation time is significant relative to the target spacing, it also
+provides less security against an attacker with a given fraction of the hash
+power.
+
+Wallets that select an anchor three blocks behind the chain tip, as
+recommended by ZIP 315 [^zip-0315], select one about 30 seconds old. A rollback
+past the anchor invalidates the transaction, and links its revealed nullifiers
+to any later transaction that spends the same notes. More frequent blocks also
+give observers finer timing information.
+
+
+# Deployment
+
+This proposal is intended to be deployed in NU8. The NU8 deployment ZIP will
+specify $\mathsf{NU8ActivationHeight}$ for each network.
+
+
+# References
+
+[^BCP14]: [Information on BCP 14 — "RFC 2119: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels" and "RFC 8174: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words"](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp14)
+
+[^protocol]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0 or later](protocol/protocol.pdf)
+
+[^protocol-networks]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0. Section 3.12: Mainnet and Testnet](protocol/protocol.pdf#networks)
+
+[^protocol-constants]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0. Section 5.3: Constants](protocol/protocol.pdf#constants)
+
+[^protocol-blockheader]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0. Section 7.6: Block Header Encoding and Consensus](protocol/protocol.pdf#blockheader)
+
+[^protocol-diffadjustment]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0. Section 7.7.3: Difficulty adjustment](protocol/protocol.pdf#diffadjustment)
+
+[^zip-0200]: [ZIP 200: Network Upgrade Mechanism](zip-0200.rst)
+
+[^zip-0207]: [ZIP 207: Funding Streams](zip-0207.rst)
+
+[^zip-0214]: [ZIP 214: Consensus rules for a Zcash Development Fund](zip-0214.rst)
+
+[^zip-0218]: [ZIP 218: 25-second Block Target Spacing](zip-0218.md)
+
+[^zip-0237]: [ZIP 237: Network Sustainability Mechanism: Halving-Preserving Issuance](zip-0237.md)
+
+[^zip-0259]: [ZIP 259: Deployment of the NU7 Network Upgrade](zip-0259.md)

+

@@ -0,0 +1,389 @@
+    ZIP: Unassigned
+    Title: Compact Block Relay
+    Owners: Marek <marek@zfnd.org>
+    Status: Draft
+    Category: Network
+    Created: 2026-10-30
+    License: MIT
+    Discussions-To: <https://github.com/zcash/zips/issues/360>
+
+
+# Terminology
+
+The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "SHOULD", and "MAY" in this document are to
+be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [^BCP14] when, and only when, they appear
+in all capitals.
+
+The terms "Mainnet" and "Testnet" are to be interpreted as described in
+section 3.12 of the Zcash Protocol Specification. [^protocol-networks]
+
+The terms "txid", "authorizing data commitment" (denoted `auth_digest`), and
+"witnessed transaction identifier" ("wtxid") are to be interpreted as
+described in ZIP 239. [^zip-0239]
+
+best tip
+:   The tip of a node's best fully validated block chain.
+
+early relay
+:   Announcing or sending a block before the sending node has fully validated
+    it.
+
+authenticated block
+:   A block that passes the checks in [Early Relay].
+
+
+# Abstract
+
+This ZIP specifies compact block relay for the Zcash peer-to-peer network,
+adapted from BIP 152. [^bip-0152] A compact block contains the block header,
+short identifiers for the block's transactions, and its coinbase transaction;
+the receiver reconstructs the block from transactions it already has. Peers
+that both opt in may also relay a block before fully validating it, once its
+header and transaction commitments have been checked.
+
+
+# Motivation
+
+As in Bitcoin before BIP 152, a Zcash node announces a block only after fully
+validating it, and a peer that requests the block receives every transaction
+in it, although it has usually already received most of them through
+transaction relay. Both delay the propagation of new blocks between miners.
+
+BIP 152 replaces transactions the receiver already has with short
+identifiers, and allows a block to be relayed before it is fully validated.
+It cannot be used in Zcash unchanged: Zcash block headers include an Equihash
+solution, and since NU5 a transaction's txid does not commit to its
+authorizing data [^zip-0244], so short identifiers and the checks made before
+early relay need to cover the wtxid.
+
+
+# Specification
+
+All messages defined in this ZIP are serialized in the standard encoding for
+P2P messages. [^zip-0204]
+
+## Service Flag
+
+The service flag `NODE_COMPACT_BLOCKS` is defined as bit 16
+(`0x0000000000010000`). This value is subject to confirmation by the ZIP
+Editors.
+
+A node that sets `NODE_COMPACT_BLOCKS` in its `version` message supports the
+messages defined in this ZIP and follows the rules in [Early Relay] and
+[Peer Misbehaviour].
+
+The messages defined in this ZIP MUST NOT be sent on a connection unless both
+peers set `NODE_COMPACT_BLOCKS` in their `version` messages, and MUST NOT be
+sent before the `version`/`verack` handshake completes. Support MUST NOT be
+inferred from any other source, such as `addr` records, user agents, or
+protocol versions. A node MUST ignore these messages on other connections.
+
+## `sendcmpct`
+
+The `sendcmpct` message is defined as a message where the `command` field is
+(NUL-padded) `"sendcmpct"`, with the following payload:
+
+| Bytes | Name | Data Type | Description |
+|-------|------|-----------|-------------|
+| 1 | `announce` | `uint8` | 1 to request `cmpctblock` announcements, 0 to stop them. |
+| 8 | `version` | `uint64` | Compact block encoding version. |
+
+This ZIP specifies version 1. A message with `announce` other than 0 or 1 is
+malformed.
+
+A node MAY send `cmpctblock` messages to a peer only while the most recent
+`sendcmpct` received from that peer has `announce` = 1 and `version` = 1. A
+`sendcmpct` with any other version disables announcements to its sender, and
+is not a protocol violation.
+
+A node MUST NOT request announcements from more than three peers at a time. It
+SHOULD request them from the peers that most recently first announced blocks
+it then added to its best chain; announcements of blocks it has not validated
+MUST NOT be counted. A node MUST ignore `cmpctblock` messages it has not
+requested. Disabling announcements MUST NOT cancel an outstanding
+`getblocktxn` request.
+
+There is no low-bandwidth mode and no compact block inventory type. Blocks
+are requested with `getdata` and `MSG_BLOCK`, as before.
+
+## `cmpctblock`
+
+The `cmpctblock` message is defined as a message where the `command` field is
+(NUL-padded) `"cmpctblock"`, with the following payload:
+
+| Bytes | Name | Data Type | Description |
+|-------|------|-----------|-------------|
+| varies | `header` | Block header | Encoded as in section 7.6 of the Zcash Protocol Specification. [^protocol-blockheader] |
+| 8 | `nonce` | `uint64` | Nonce used to compute short IDs. |
+| varies | `shortidsCount` | `CompactSize` | Number of short IDs. |
+| `6 * shortidsCount` | `shortids` | `uint8[6][]` | Short IDs of the transactions that are not prefilled, in block order. |
+| varies | `prefilledCount` | `CompactSize` | Number of prefilled transactions. |
+| varies | `prefilled` | `PrefilledTransaction[]` | Prefilled transactions, in block order. |
+
+The header includes the Equihash solution, and does not include the
+transaction count that follows it in a `headers` message. On Mainnet and
+Testnet it is 1,487 bytes.
+
+A `PrefilledTransaction` has the following format:
+
+| Bytes | Name | Data Type | Description |
+|-------|------|-----------|-------------|
+| varies | `index` | `CompactSize` | Differentially encoded index of the transaction in the block. |
+| varies | `tx` | Transaction | The transaction, encoded as in section 7.1 of the Zcash Protocol Specification. [^protocol-txnencoding] |
+
+In a list of differentially encoded indexes, the first entry is the absolute
+index, and each later entry is the absolute index minus the previous absolute
+index minus 1. For example, `[0, 0, 2]` encodes the absolute indexes
+`[0, 1, 4]`. Counts and indexes MUST be checked before allocation or
+indexing, and count addition and index decoding MUST NOT overflow.
+
+Let `n = shortidsCount + prefilledCount` be the number of transactions in the
+block. A node MUST reject a `cmpctblock` message if:
+
+- any of `shortidsCount`, `prefilledCount`, and `n` exceeds 37,037;
+- the absolute prefilled indexes are not strictly increasing, or any is not
+  less than `n`;
+- the first prefilled transaction is not a coinbase transaction at index 0,
+  or any other prefilled transaction is a coinbase transaction; or
+- the sizes of the header, the `CompactSize` encoding of `n`, and the
+  prefilled transactions, plus 54 bytes for each short ID, sum to more than
+  2,000,000 bytes.
+
+Senders SHOULD prefill only the coinbase transaction.
+
+### Short Transaction IDs
+
+The sender SHOULD choose `nonce` uniformly at random for each `cmpctblock`
+message. The short ID of a transaction is computed as follows:
+
+1. Let `h` be the SHA-256 hash of the encoded block header followed by
+   `nonce`.
+2. Let `k0` and `k1` be bytes 0 to 7 and 8 to 15 of `h`, each interpreted as
+   a little-endian `uint64`.
+3. Compute SipHash-2-4 with keys `(k0, k1)` of the transaction's 32-byte txid
+   for v4 and earlier transactions, or of its 64-byte wtxid for v5 and later
+   transactions.
+4. The short ID is the first 6 bytes of the little-endian encoding of the
+   result.
+
+## `getblocktxn` and `blocktxn`
+
+The `getblocktxn` message is defined as a message where the `command` field
+is (NUL-padded) `"getblocktxn"`, with the following payload:
+
+| Bytes | Name | Data Type | Description |
+|-------|------|-----------|-------------|
+| 32 | `blockHash` | `uint8[32]` | Hash of the block announced by `cmpctblock`. |
+| varies | `indexesCount` | `CompactSize` | Number of requested transactions. |
+| varies | `indexes` | `CompactSize[]` | Differentially encoded indexes of the requested transactions. |
+
+The `indexesCount` field MUST NOT exceed 37,037, and the absolute indexes
+MUST be strictly increasing and less than `n`.
+
+The `blocktxn` message is defined as a message where the `command` field is
+(NUL-padded) `"blocktxn"`, with the following payload:
+
+| Bytes | Name | Data Type | Description |
+|-------|------|-----------|-------------|
+| 32 | `blockHash` | `uint8[32]` | `blockHash` from the request. |
+| varies | `txCount` | `CompactSize` | Number of transactions. |
+| varies | `tx` | Transaction[] | The requested transactions, in the order requested. |
+
+A `blocktxn` message MUST contain exactly the requested transactions, which
+MUST NOT exceed 2,000,000 bytes in total.
+
+A node that sends a `cmpctblock` message MUST be able to answer a
+`getblocktxn` request for any subset of the block's transactions, and SHOULD
+retain the block for this purpose for 15 seconds. It SHOULD limit the
+`blocktxn` messages it sends for one `cmpctblock` message, including repeated
+and empty responses, to 2,000,000 bytes in total, and MAY ignore requests
+beyond that limit or after that time. It MUST ignore requests for blocks it
+has not announced on that connection or no longer retains, and requests for
+indexes outside the block.
+
+A node MUST ignore a `blocktxn` message that does not answer its outstanding
+`getblocktxn` request on that connection, and SHOULD wait at most two seconds
+for the answer.
+
+## Sending Compact Blocks
+
+A node MUST send each block announcement as `cmpctblock` to at most three
+peers, and SHOULD do so only when the `cmpctblock` message is smaller than the
+block. Other peers receive the announcement as before. A node MAY announce a
+fully validated block with `cmpctblock` to any peer that requested
+announcements.
+
+### Early Relay
+
+A node MAY relay a block before fully validating it only to peers that set
+`NODE_COMPACT_BLOCKS`, and only after checking that:
+
+- NU5 is active at the block's height;
+- the block's parent is the node's best tip, and the block's coinbase height
+  is one more than the best tip's height;
+- the header has the expected difficulty, a valid Equihash solution, a hash
+  that meets its target, and a valid time with respect to both the local
+  clock and the median time past;
+- the block is at most 2,000,000 bytes, its first transaction is a coinbase
+  transaction, and no later transaction has a transparent input with a null
+  previous output;
+- the block passes the shielded action limits, and the subsidy and funding
+  stream checks that do not depend on value pool state;
+- the txids are distinct and reproduce `hashMerkleRoot`, and each
+  transaction's consensus branch ID is valid at the block's height;
+- the `auth_digest` values of all transactions reproduce the authorizing data
+  root, which together with the parent's chain history reproduces
+  `hashBlockCommitments`, as specified in ZIP 244; [^zip-0244] and
+- the block has not been rejected or invalidated by the node.
+
+While it completes validation, the node MAY announce the block, and MAY answer
+`getdata` requests for it from those peers. It MUST stop early relay of the
+block when its validation fails or is cancelled, or when its parent is no
+longer the best tip, and MUST check these conditions before sending each
+message. It SHOULD continue to answer `getblocktxn` requests for a
+`cmpctblock` message it has already sent.
+
+## Receiving Compact Blocks
+
+Before retaining a `cmpctblock` message or querying its mempool, a node MUST
+check the coinbase height, NU5 activation, the header's time, target, and
+proof of work, and that the block's parent is its best tip. If these checks
+fail, the node SHOULD treat the message as an announcement of the block hash.
+A node SHOULD limit the compact blocks it retains and the `getblocktxn`
+requests it sends, both per peer and in total.
+
+The node then reconstructs the block:
+
+1. Place the prefilled transactions at their indexes.
+2. For each index that is not prefilled, if its short ID occurs only once in
+   the message and exactly one mempool transaction has that short ID, place
+   that transaction at the index.
+3. If any index remains empty, send one `getblocktxn` request for all of
+   them.
+4. Check that the `blocktxn` response contains one transaction for each
+   requested index, with the corresponding short ID.
+5. Check the block size, the coinbase transaction, that the txids are
+   distinct and reproduce `hashMerkleRoot`, and that the `auth_digest` values
+   reproduce the commitments as in [Early Relay], then fully validate the
+   block.
+
+Step 5 is required because a short ID can match the wrong transaction, and
+`hashMerkleRoot` does not commit to authorizing data.
+
+If any step fails, or the response does not arrive in time, the node MUST
+request the block from the same peer with `getdata` and `MSG_BLOCK`, using its
+usual timeout. A reconstruction failure MUST NOT cause the node to treat the
+block as invalid.
+
+## Peer Misbehaviour
+
+A node MAY treat a malformed message defined in this ZIP as it treats other
+malformed P2P messages. This includes non-canonical `CompactSize` encodings,
+indexes out of range, and counts or sizes that exceed the limits above.
+
+A node MUST NOT penalize a peer for short ID collisions, failed
+reconstructions, commitment mismatches in reconstructed blocks, `blocktxn`
+timeouts, or an unknown parent.
+
+A node MUST NOT penalize a peer that set `NODE_COMPACT_BLOCKS` when an
+authenticated block it sent fails later validation; the node still rejects
+the block. A node MAY penalize a peer that sends a full block failing the
+proof of work, size, structure, or commitment checks in [Early Relay]. If the
+node cannot authenticate a block because the parent's chain history is
+unavailable, but the block passes the checks that do not depend on it, the
+node MUST NOT penalize the peer for a later transaction or contextual
+validation failure. Failures of local time policy and local invalidation are
+not peer misbehaviour.
+
+## Deployment
+
+This ZIP applies on Mainnet and Testnet from NU5 activation. It does not
+require a network upgrade. Peers that do not set `NODE_COMPACT_BLOCKS` use
+block relay as before.
+
+
+# Rationale
+
+This ZIP differs from BIP 152 as follows:
+
+- The header is the Zcash block header, including the Equihash solution.
+- Short IDs are computed from the wtxid for v5 and later transactions, so
+  version 1 of the encoding is not Bitcoin's version 1.
+- Only high-bandwidth announcements are defined.
+- Support is signalled by a service flag rather than a protocol version, and
+  an unsupported version disables announcements rather than being negotiated.
+- The coinbase transaction is always prefilled, and all counts and sizes are
+  bounded.
+- Early relay requires checking authorizing data, and is limited to children
+  of the best tip.
+
+Zebra and zcashd ignore unknown P2P messages after the handshake
+[^zebra-codec] [^zcashd-messages], so a service flag is not needed to avoid
+disconnection. It is needed because both peers have to agree on the encoding,
+and on not penalizing authenticated blocks that fail later validation; an
+ignored message establishes neither. A protocol version signals support for a
+network upgrade, not for an optional relay policy. [^zip-0201]
+
+The limit of 37,037 transactions is the 2,000,000-byte block size limit
+divided by 54 bytes, a lower bound on the size of a transaction.
+
+Bit 16 avoids the service flags allocated in Zcash and Bitcoin
+[^bitcoin-services], the range 24 to 31 reserved for temporary experiments,
+and bits 12 to 14, which are used by pending Bitcoin proposals.
+[^bitcoin-utreexo] [^bitcoin-utxo-sharing]
+
+
+# Security and Privacy Considerations
+
+A short ID identifies a transaction only probabilistically. A node that
+skipped the checks in step 5 of [Receiving Compact Blocks] could accept a
+block whose authorizing data differs from the data committed to by its
+header.
+
+An early relayed block can be invalid. Receiving one does not indicate that
+the block is valid, and nodes MUST fully validate it before accepting it.
+
+A `getblocktxn` request reveals which transactions the sender did not have,
+and the timing of announcements can reveal a node's peers. Setting
+`NODE_COMPACT_BLOCKS` reveals that a node supports this ZIP.
+
+
+# Reference Implementation
+
+Zebra implements this ZIP behind the default-off option
+`experimental_early_block_relay`, using temporary service bit 25. [^zebra] It
+will use the bit confirmed for this ZIP; until then, it does not negotiate
+compact block relay with peers that use the confirmed bit.
+
+
+# References
+

+
+[^protocol-networks]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0 [NU6.3]. Section 3.12: Mainnet and Testnet](protocol/protocol.pdf#networks)
+
+[^protocol-txnencoding]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0 [NU6.3]. Section 7.1: Transaction Encoding and Consensus](protocol/protocol.pdf#txnencoding)
+
+[^protocol-blockheader]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0 [NU6.3]. Section 7.6: Block Header Encoding and Consensus](protocol/protocol.pdf#blockheader)
+
+[^zip-0201]: [ZIP 201: Network Peer Management for Overwinter](zip-0201.rst)
+
+[^zip-0204]: [ZIP 204: Zcash P2P Network Protocol](zip-0204.rst)
+
+[^zip-0239]: [ZIP 239: Relay of Version 5 Transactions](zip-0239.rst)
+
+[^zip-0244]: [ZIP 244: Transaction Identifier Non-Malleability](zip-0244.rst)
+
+[^bip-0152]: [BIP 152: Compact Block Relay](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0152.mediawiki)
+
+[^zebra]: [Zebra, revision 4b8a202e41d41b8ab84a703c72ef77fd03d4d000](https://github.com/ZcashFoundation/zebra/tree/4b8a202e41d41b8ab84a703c72ef77fd03d4d000)

This starts the migration of remaining Sapling funds into quantum-recoverable pools, mirroring ZIP 211 for Sprout and the NU6.3 rule for Orchard. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01YAZUfBjv73EbfdP4vfHiyn --- README.rst | 1 + ...aft-valargroup-sapling-disable-deposits.md | 336 ++++++++++++++++++ 2 files changed, 337 insertions(+) create mode 100644 zips/draft-valargroup-sapling-disable-deposits.md diff --git a/README.rst b/README.rst index 1ded627f1..abbcfe093 100644 --- a/README.rst +++ b/README.rst @@ -235,6 +235,7 @@ be deleted. draft-ecc-onchain-accountable-voting On-chain Accountable Voting draft-mcgee-keyholders-organizations Update to ZIP 1016 & ZIP 271: Key-Holder Organizations URL TBD draft-str4d-orchard-balance-proof Air drops, Proof-of-Balance, and Stake-weighted Polling zips#1229 + draft-valargroup-sapling-disable-deposits Disabling Sapling Pool Deposits https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/sapling-withdraw-only-discussion-kickoff/55223 Withdrawn, Rejected, or Obsolete ZIPs diff --git a/zips/draft-valargroup-sapling-disable-deposits.md b/zips/draft-valargroup-sapling-disable-deposits.md new file mode 100644 index 000000000..3d85fcd79 --- /dev/null +++ b/zips/draft-valargroup-sapling-disable-deposits.md @@ -0,0 +1,336 @@ + ZIP: Unassigned + Title: Disabling Sapling Pool Deposits + Owners: Dev Ojha + Status: Draft + Category: Consensus / Wallet + Created: 2026-10-27 + License: MIT + Discussions-To: + Pull-Request: + + +# Terminology + +The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", and "MAY" in this +document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [^BCP14] when, and only +when, they appear in all capitals. + +The term "network upgrade" in this document is to be interpreted as described +in ZIP 200. [^zip-0200] + +The character § is used when referring to sections of the Zcash Protocol +Specification. [^protocol] + +The terms "Mainnet" and "Testnet" are to be interpreted as described in +§ 3.12 ‘Mainnet and Testnet’. [^protocol-networks] + +The term "Sapling shielded protocol" refers to the shielded payment protocol +introduced in the Sapling network upgrade. [^zip-0205] Following the +convention of ZIP 229 [^zip-0229], *Sapling pool*, *Orchard pool* and +*Ironwood pool* refer to chain value pools, as distinct from the protocols that +operate on them. + +The term "Sapling chain value pool balance" is to be interpreted as described +in ZIP 209 [^zip-0209] and § 4.17 ‘Chain Value Pool Balances’. +[^protocol-chainvaluepoolbalances] + +The term "quantum recoverable" is to be interpreted as described in +ZIP 2005. [^zip-2005] + +NU8 refers to the network upgrade following NU7. + + +# Abstract + +This proposal disables the ability to add new value to the *Sapling pool*, +making it withdraw-only. From NU8 activation, every transaction's Sapling value +balance must be nonnegative: value may leave the *Sapling pool*, or move between +Sapling notes, but no new value may enter it. Coinbase transactions may no +longer contain Sapling outputs. + +This starts the migration of the remaining *Sapling pool* funds into +quantum-recoverable shielded pools (the *Ironwood pool* today, and Tachyon +once deployed). It is the Sapling counterpart of what ZIP 211 [^zip-0211] did +for Sprout at Canopy and what NU6.3 [^zip-0258] did for the *Orchard pool*. + + +# Motivation + +The Sapling shielded protocol is not quantum recoverable: an adversary able to +compute discrete logarithms, for example with a quantum computer, could steal +funds held in the *Sapling pool*. ZIP 2005 expects Sapling funds to be +migrated to the *Ironwood pool* instead [^zip-2005]. Ironwood notes are quantum +recoverable, and formal verification shows that undetectable counterfeiting +bugs do not exist in Ironwood. [^Ironwood-book] [^ironwood-verification] +Ironwood and later Tachyon [^tachyon] are steps toward a fully post-quantum +shielded pool soon after. + +Nothing currently stops new value from entering the *Sapling pool*, and every +deposit adds to what must later be migrated. Pool migrations take years: about +22,000 ZEC remains in Sprout six years after ZIP 211 made it withdraw-only +[^zip-0211]. The *Sapling pool* holds about 419,900 ZEC, or 8.5% of shielded +ZEC [^cipherscan-supply]. Disabling deposits now, while all funds remain fully +spendable, gives custodians and wallets a firm deadline and makes the +remaining balance only decline. + +The cost of doing so is low. Excluding mining pool coinbase shielding and the +Zcash Community Grants funding stream, which can move to Ironwood (see Open +issues), only 1.2% of non-coinbase transactions in the last 30 days touched +the *Sapling pool*, and they withdrew 101,216 ZEC more than they deposited. +Coinbase outputs to Sapling are essentially unused. [^sapling-activity] + +As with Sprout [^zip-0211], disabling additions also limits the impact of any +undiscovered soundness bug in Sapling, and is a precondition for eventually +removing the Sapling shielded protocol. + + +# Requirements + +* No new value can enter the *Sapling pool* after activation, from any + transaction version, including coinbase. +* Holders keep full access to their Sapling funds. They can spend to any + other pool (in practice Ironwood or transparent), and can keep making + Sapling-to-Sapling transfers, including to other people. +* No change to the Sapling circuits or parameters, and no new trusted setup. +* The consensus change is small and easy to analyse. + + +# Non-requirements + +* This ZIP does not set a date after which Sapling notes can no longer be + spent. That is left to a future proposal. So is what happens to any value + left in the pool at that point. +* This ZIP does not make Sapling quantum recoverable. +* This ZIP does not restrict the *Sprout pool* or the transparent pool. + + +# Specification + +## Consensus rules + +The following rules apply to every transaction in a block at a height greater +than or equal to the NU8 activation height, regardless of transaction version: + +* The Sapling value balance of the transaction MUST be nonnegative. For + version 4, 5 and 6 transactions, `valueBalanceSapling` MUST be greater than + or equal to zero. As before, it is taken to be zero when absent. For a + transaction format that expresses value balances as value pool deltas + [^zip-0248], the delta for the Sapling bundle and the ZEC asset MUST be + greater than or equal to zero. + +* A coinbase transaction MUST NOT contain any Sapling Output descriptions; + that is, `nOutputsSapling` MUST be zero. Coinbase transactions are already + required to have `nSpendsSapling` equal to zero. + +Non-normative notes: + +* `valueBalanceSapling` is the value of Sapling Spends minus Outputs. When it + is nonnegative, value can only move out of the *Sapling pool* or stay inside + it. Together with the ZIP 209 [^zip-0209] rule that the Sapling chain value + pool balance never goes negative, the balance can only stay the same or fall + from activation onward. + +* Sapling Output descriptions remain valid in non-coinbase transactions. A + transaction may pay Sapling notes to any Sapling address, including a third + party's, if Sapling spends in the same transaction fund those outputs. + +* The coinbase rule is partly implied by the balance rule, because a coinbase + transaction has no Sapling spends. It is stated explicitly so that + zero-valued Sapling coinbase outputs are excluded too, and to mirror the + NU6.3 rule for the *Orchard pool* [^zip-0258]. + +## Changes to ZIP 213 + +In the Specification section of ZIP 213 [^zip-0213], after the NU6.3 rules, +add: + +> Once the NU8 network upgrade activates: +> +> - Coinbase transactions MAY contain *Ironwood-pool* outputs. +> - Coinbase transactions MUST NOT contain Sapling outputs. + +## Changes to the Protocol Specification + +§ 7.1.2 ‘Transaction Consensus Rules’ [^protocol-txnconsensus] gains the two +consensus rules above, gated on NU8 activation, alongside the existing NU6.3 +rule that $\mathsf{v}^{\textit{OrchardPoolBalance}}$ is nonnegative. + +## Requirements for wallets and node software + +From NU8 activation: + +* Wallets MUST NOT create transactions that contain one or more Sapling + outputs together with one or more inputs from outside the *Sapling pool* + (transparent inputs, or spends from any other shielded pool). As with + ZIP 211 [^zip-0211], this is stricter than consensus, for usability + reasons. Consensus would accept a mixed transaction whose Sapling spends + cover its Sapling outputs. + +* When a payment is to a Sapling-only address and the wallet cannot fund it + entirely from Sapling notes, the wallet MUST refuse it. The error MUST say + that the *Sapling pool* no longer accepts deposits. It SHOULD suggest asking + the recipient for a Unified Address with an Orchard-protocol receiver. + +* When a payment is to a Unified Address that has both a Sapling receiver + and an Orchard-protocol receiver, wallets SHOULD pay to the *Ironwood pool*. + They MUST do so unless the payment is funded entirely from Sapling notes. + +* Wallets SHOULD NOT create new Unified Addresses that include a Sapling + receiver. They MAY keep producing Sapling receivers before activation for + compatibility. + +* Wallets that hold Sapling funds SHOULD offer to migrate them to the + *Ironwood pool*, and SHOULD do so before activation. Wallets SHOULD use + migration strategies that limit linkability of the amounts moved, in the + spirit of ZIP 308 [^zip-0308] and ZIP 318 [^zip-0318]. Migration into the + *Orchard pool* is already not possible. + +* Block template software MUST NOT produce coinbase transactions with Sapling + outputs, and SHOULD reject Sapling-only miner addresses with a clear error. + +Software SHOULD make these changes clear in user interfaces and API +documentation before activation. + +Transactions signed for an earlier consensus branch become invalid at NU8 +activation under ZIP 200 [^zip-0200] and ZIP 244 [^zip-0244], so no +mempool-specific rule is needed. + + +# Rationale + +## Why a balance rule, not a circuit change + +The rule mirrors ZIP 211 for Sprout and the NU6.3 rule for Orchard. It only +needs a check on a field validators already parse. It does not touch the +Sapling Spend or Output circuits. That avoids a new parameter generation +ceremony, any risk of a soundness regression in Groth16 circuits, and any new +transaction version. The implementation is a few lines in each full validator, +and its security is easy to analyse. + +## Why internal transfers stay allowed + +NU6.3 also disabled cross-address transfers within the *Orchard pool*. That +was possible because the new Orchard Action circuit had an `enableCrossAddress` +flag [^zip-2006]. Doing the same for Sapling would need a new Sapling circuit +and trusted setup, which this ZIP sets out to avoid. + +Allowing Sapling outputs also lets wallets keep using Sapling change when +withdrawing, so a withdrawal reveals only the amount leaving the pool rather +than the total value of the notes spent. + +## Why the coinbase prohibition is explicit + +ZIP 213 has allowed coinbase outputs to Sapling addresses since Heartwood +[^zip-0213], but miners have not adopted it: only one Mainnet block has ever +paid its coinbase to a Sapling output. {TODO: cite the block height and txid.} +Shielded coinbase has instead moved to the Orchard protocol, which since NU6.3 +pays into the *Ironwood pool*. Users with +large Sapling balances SHOULD migrate in several transactions spread over time. + +As users leave, the *Sapling pool* anonymity set will shrink. Users who stay +in it get progressively less privacy, and wallets SHOULD tell them so. Note +that the effective anonymity set is already much smaller than the pool's +transaction count suggests: most Sapling transactions today are mining pool +and funding stream coinbase sweeps whose source is publicly known, and many +of them are round trips back to the same transparent address (see +[Open issues](#open-issues)). prs.author: daira
prs.bodyExcerpt: Fixes #1417. ZIP 221's "Tree Node specification" said that `CONSENSUS_BRANCH_ID` in the personalization is the branch ID "for the epoch of the block containing the commitment". At the activation block of a network upgrade after Heartwood, that reads as the new epoch's branch ID. The pseudocode (`mak

From 5b7a5e49fdbfaae398ed0ccb1147b3869a72cb19 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Daira-Emma Hopwood <daira@jacaranda.org>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 07:46:09 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] ZIP 221: say which epoch's branch ID personalizes the root at
 an activation block

The prose said the branch ID of "the epoch of the block containing the commitment".
At the activation block of a network upgrade after Heartwood, that reads as the new
epoch's branch ID. The pseudocode hashes the root with the branch ID of the leaves,
which is the previous epoch's, and zcashd and Zebra do the same. Say so.

Fixes #1417.

Co-authored-by: Claude Mythos 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
---
 zips/zip-0221.rst | 8 +++++---
 1 file changed, 5 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)

diff --git a/zips/zip-0221.rst b/zips/zip-0221.rst
index 4ee35acce..5d63d77a1 100644
--- a/zips/zip-0221.rst
+++ b/zips/zip-0221.rst
@@ -188,9 +188,11 @@ Tree Node specification
 
 Unless otherwise noted, all hashes use BLAKE2b-256 with the personalization field set
 to ``'ZcashHistory' || CONSENSUS_BRANCH_ID``. ``CONSENSUS_BRANCH_ID`` is the 4-byte
-little-endian encoding of the consensus branch ID for the epoch of the block containing
-the commitment. [#zip-0200]_ Which is to say, each node in the tree commits to the
-consensus branch that produced it.
+little-endian encoding of the consensus branch ID for the epoch of the blocks that the
+tree covers. [#zip-0200]_ That is, each node in the tree commits to the consensus
+branch that produced it. At the activation block of a network upgrade after
+Heartwood, the tree covers the blocks of the previous epoch, so the root commitment in
+that block's header is hashed with the consensus branch ID of the previous epoch.

 transaction format

OrchardZSA notes would be held only in the Ironwood pool. The ZIP now
says that {{ZSALEADBYTE}}, their note plaintext lead byte, is a
placeholder whose value is yet to be assigned. Quantum recoverability,
which NU6.3 deployed for the Ironwood pool, is no longer described as a
prerequisite. The ZIP is instead defined relative to a version of the
protocol specification that is yet to be determined.

ZIPs 230 and 246, which specified the ZSA transaction format and digests
for the ZIP 230 design, have been withdrawn. ZIP 248 provisionally
registers an OrchardZSA bundle variant, so the sections on transaction
structure, wallets, and sighash now refer to the transaction version
that ZIP 248 specifies. The sighash section cites ZIP 248's digest
algorithms and sighash versioning. Open Issue notes, next to the text
that relies on the ZIP 230 design, say what is yet to be specified. Each
issue is described in full where it first occurs, and later notes refer
back to it. Wallets are asked to use the OrchardZSA bundle variant for
their Ironwood-pool actions, since otherwise the privacy benefit of
indistinguishable assets does not apply. The references are updated to
match.

Subject: [PATCH 3/6] ZIPs 227, 228: Note where they rely on the withdrawn ZIP
 230 design

Open Issue notes, next to the text that relies on the ZIP 230 design,
say what is yet to be specified for the transaction format of ZIP 248.
That includes the encodings of the issuance bundle and of Action Groups,
and their digests and sighash versions. Each issue is described in full
where it first occurs, and later notes refer back to it. Supporting
Action Groups would require a modification to ZIP 248, which is possible
independently of whether ZSAs activate at the same time.

References to ZIP 246 now cite the digest algorithms, sighash
versioning, and v0 signature digest of ZIP 248, and the titles of the
ZIP 230 references are updated. ZIP 227's link to ZIP 226's TxId Digest
section, which no longer exists, now points to ZIP 227's own Sighash
section.

From fb8d546afed542ee61e7e5ee00535a04e987a9b7 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Daira-Emma Hopwood <daira@jacaranda.org>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 17:21:43 +0100
Subject: [PATCH 1/3] ZIP 221: Fix slips in the node pseudocode

The node structure declared nSaplingTxCount a second time where it
meant nOrchardTxCount, serialize read the Sapling and Orchard roots
without self, and make_parent read sapling_root and orchard_root, which
are not node fields. They now use the node's own fields.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
---
 zips/zip-0221.rst | 20 ++++++++++----------
 1 file changed, 10 insertions(+), 10 deletions(-)

diff --git a/zips/zip-0221.rst b/zips/zip-0221.rst
index 4ee35acce..1903875d5 100644
--- a/zips/zip-0221.rst
+++ b/zips/zip-0221.rst
@@ -402,7 +402,7 @@ Tree nodes and hashing (pseudocode)
         # NU5 only.
         hashEarliestOrchardRoot: Optional[bytes] # left child's Orchard root
         hashLatestOrchardRoot: Optional[bytes] # right child's Orchard root
-        nSaplingTxCount: Optional[int] # number of Orchard transactions in block
+        nOrchardTxCount: Optional[int] # number of Orchard transactions in block
 
         consensusBranchId: bytes
 
@@ -435,15 +435,15 @@ Tree nodes and hashing (pseudocode)
                 + serialize_uint32(self.nLatestTimestamp)
                 + serialize_uint32(self.nEarliestTargetBits)
                 + serialize_uint32(self.nLatestTargetBits)
-                + hashEarliestSaplingRoot
-                + hashLatestSaplingRoot
+                + self.hashEarliestSaplingRoot
+                + self.hashLatestSaplingRoot
                 + serialize_uint256(self.nSubTreeTotalWork)
                 + serialize_compact_uint(self.nEarliestHeight)
                 + serialize_compact_uint(self.nLatestHeight)
                 + serialize_compact_uint(self.nSaplingTxCount))
-            if hashEarliestOrchardRoot is not None:
-                buf += (hashEarliestOrchardRoot
-                    + hashLatestOrchardRoot
+            if self.hashEarliestOrchardRoot is not None:
+                buf += (self.hashEarliestOrchardRoot
+                    + self.hashLatestOrchardRoot
                     + serialize_compact_uint(self.nOrchardTxCount))
             return buf
 
@@ -460,14 +460,14 @@ Tree nodes and hashing (pseudocode)
             nLatestTimestamp=right_child.nLatestTimestamp,
             nEarliestTargetBits=left_child.nEarliestTargetBits,
             nLatestTargetBits=right_child.nLatestTargetBits,
-            hashEarliestSaplingRoot=left_child.sapling_root,
-            hashLatestSaplingRoot=right_child.sapling_root,
+            hashEarliestSaplingRoot=left_child.hashEarliestSaplingRoot,
+            hashLatestSaplingRoot=right_child.hashLatestSaplingRoot,
             nSubTreeTotalWork=left_child.nSubTreeTotalWork + right_child.nSubTreeTotalWork,
             nEarliestHeight=left_child.nEarliestHeight,
             nLatestHeight=right_child.nLatestHeight,
             nSaplingTxCount=left_child.nSaplingTxCount + right_child.nSaplingTxCount,
-            hashEarliestOrchardRoot=left_child.orchard_root,
-            hashLatestOrchardRoot=right_child.orchard_root,
+            hashEarliestOrchardRoot=left_child.hashEarliestOrchardRoot,
+            hashLatestOrchardRoot=right_child.hashLatestOrchardRoot,
             nOrchardTxCount=(left_child.nOrchardTxCount + right_child.nOrchardTxCount
                              if left_child.nOrchardTxCount is not None and right_child.nOrchardTxCount is not None
                              else None),

From 1b24567b2763b99f7e3d3753788e119d11b2bef3 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Daira-Emma Hopwood <daira@jacaranda.org>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 17:23:29 +0100
Subject: [PATCH 2/3] ZIP 221: Add the Ironwood fields that ZIP 258 specifies

ZIP 258, which deploys NU6.3, specifies three history tree node fields
for the Ironwood pool, mirroring the Orchard ones:
hashEarliestIronwoodRoot, hashLatestIronwoodRoot, and nIronwoodTxCount.
ZIP 221 did not have them. They are now in the Tree Node specification,
with the sentences on omitted fields and node sizes, and in the
pseudocode.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
---
 zips/zip-0221.rst | 58 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++----
 1 file changed, 54 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)

diff --git a/zips/zip-0221.rst b/zips/zip-0221.rst
index 1903875d5..8ca7a6dc7 100644
--- a/zips/zip-0221.rst
+++ b/zips/zip-0221.rst
@@ -362,13 +362,47 @@ Each MMR node is defined as follows:
 
     Serialized as ``CompactSize uint``.
 
+15. [NU6.3 onward] ``hashEarliestIronwoodRoot``
 
-The fields marked "[NU5 onward]" are omitted before NU5 activation [#zip-0252]_.
+    Leaf node
+      Calculated as the note commitment root of the final Ironwood treestate
+      (similar to ``hashEarliestOrchardRoot``).
+
+    Internal or root node
+      Inherited from the left child.
+
+    Serialized as ``char[32]``.
+
+16. [NU6.3 onward] ``hashLatestIronwoodRoot``
+
+    Leaf node
+      Calculated as the note commitment root of the final Ironwood treestate
+      (similar to ``hashLatestOrchardRoot``).
+
+    Internal or root node
+      Inherited from the right child.
+
+    Serialized as ``char[32]``.
+
+17. [NU6.3 onward] ``nIronwoodTxCount``
+
+    Leaf node
+      The number of transactions in the leaf block where ``vActionsIronwood``
+      is non-empty.
+
+    Internal or root node
+      The sum of the ``nIronwoodTxCount`` field of both children.
+
+    Serialized as ``CompactSize uint``.
+
+
+The fields marked "[NU5 onward]" are omitted before NU5 activation [#zip-0252]_. The
+fields marked "[NU6.3 onward]" are omitted before NU6.3 activation.
 
 Each node, when serialized, is between 147 and 171 bytes long (between 212 and 244 bytes
-after NU5 activation). The canonical serialized representation of a node is used whenever

-receives an arbitrary-sized byte string and returns a Scalar. It is defined
-concretely in the Ciphersuites section.
-

 --------------
@@ -160,10 +156,71 @@ To add re-randomization to FROST, follow the specification [#FROST]_ with the
 following modifications.
 
 
+Randomizer Generation
+'''''''''''''''''''''
+
+Two new helper functions are defined, which generate a randomizer; the first is
+used by the Coordinator and the second is used by participants. The
+`encode_signing_commitments` function SHOULD return the byte serialization of
+the `commitment_list` value as the serialization of the map between identifiers
+and signing commitments, as described in [#frost-serialization]_.
+Implementations MAY choose another encoding as long as all values (the
+identifier, binding nonce and hiding nonce for each participant) are
+unambiguously encoded.
+
+The function `random_bytes(n)` is defined in [#FROST]_ and it returns a buffer
+with `n` bytes sampled uniformly at random. The constant `Ns` is also specified
+in [#FROST]_ and is the size of a serialized scalar. The function `H2(m)` is a
+ciphersuite-generic function defined in [#FROST]_ but instantiated in the
+Ciphersuites section.
+
+::
+
+  randomizer_generate():
+
+  Inputs:
+  - commitment_list = [(i, hiding_nonce_commitment_i,
+    binding_nonce_commitment_i), ...], a list of commitments issued by
+    each participant, where each element in the list indicates a
+    NonZeroScalar identifier i and two commitment Element values
+    (hiding_nonce_commitment_i, binding_nonce_commitment_i). This list
+    MUST be sorted in ascending order by identifier.
+
+  Outputs: (randomizer_seed, randomizer), a byte buffer and a Scalar
+
+  def randomizer_generate(commitment_list):
+    # Generate a random byte buffer with the size of a serialized scalar
+    randomizer_seed = random_bytes(Ns)
+    signing_commitments_enc = encode_signing_commitments(commitment_list)
+    randomizer_input = randomizer_seed || signing_commitments_enc
+    return (randomizer_seed, H2(randomizer_input))
+
+::
+
+  randomizer_regenerate():
+
+  Inputs:
+  - randomizer_seed = a byte buffer with Ns bytes
+  - commitment_list = [(i, hiding_nonce_commitment_i,
+    binding_nonce_commitment_i), ...], a list of commitments issued by
+    each participant, where each element in the list indicates a
+    NonZeroScalar identifier i and two commitment Element values
+    (hiding_nonce_commitment_i, binding_nonce_commitment_i). This list
+    MUST be sorted in ascending order by identifier.
+
+  Outputs: randomizer, a Scalar
+
+  def randomizer_generate(randomizer_seed, commitment_list):
+    signing_commitments_enc = encode_signing_commitments(commitment_list)
+    randomizer_input = randomizer_seed || signing_commitments_enc

+

 ''''''''''''''''''''''
 
-Roune One is exactly the same as specified [#FROST]_. But for context, it
+Round One is exactly the same as specified [#FROST]_. But for context, it

+each signer along with the commitments received in Round One. In Re-Randomized
+FROST, the Coordinator MUST additionally call `randomizer_generate` and send the
+`randomizer_seed` along with the message and the commitments. Each participant,
+upon receiving those values, MUST compute `randomizer` by calling
+`randomizer_regenerate` with the received `randomizer_seed` and commitments.
 
 In Zcash, the message that needs to be signed is actually the SIGHASH
 transaction hash, which does not convey enough information for the signers to
@@ -191,14 +249,6 @@ that the given SIGHASH matches the data sent from the Coordinator, or compute th
 SIGHASH themselves from that data. However, the specific mechanism for that process
 is outside the scope of this ZIP.
 
-In Zcash, the `randomizer` is called :math:`\mathsf{alpha}` and MUST be
-generated accordingly to the Zcash specification [#protocol-spendauthsig]_. Note
-that the choice of :math:`\mathsf{alpha}` influences the SIGHASH computation, so
-it is impossible to compute the `randomizer` based on the message (SIGHASH), as
-suggested in [#frost-rerandomized]_. This is not an issue as long the
-`randomizer` is generated uniformly at random, which is done in the Zcash
-specification.
-
 The randomized ``sign`` function is defined as the regular FROST ``sign``
 function, but with its inputs modified relative to the ``randomizer`` as
 following:
@@ -393,6 +443,22 @@ signing generates a re-randomized signature:
 The security of Re-Randomized FROST with respect to the security assumptions of
 regular FROST is shown in [#frost-rerandomized]_.
 
+Regarding randomizer handling, in Zcash, the `randomizer` is called
+:math:`\mathsf{alpha}` and is usually generated using the `RedDSA.GenRandom`
+function as defined inthe  Zcash specification [#protocol-spendauthsig]_. Note
+that the choice of :math:`\mathsf{alpha}` influences the SIGHASH computation, so
+it is impossible to compute the `randomizer` based on the message (SIGHASH), as
+suggested in [#frost-rerandomized]_. This is not an issue as long the
+`randomizer` is generated with the same security properties as
+`RedDSA.GenRandom`. We ensure that by using a very similar approach; while the
+original `RedDSA.GenRandom` uses :math:`\mathsf{H}^\circledast(T)` where T is a
+random byte buffer with a certain size, in this ZIP we effectively use
+:math:`\mathsf{H}^\circledast(T || signing_commitments_enc)`, i.e. we
+concatenate the random bytes with the encoding of the signing commitments. This
+preserves the security assumptions and also hedges against issues in the
+Coordinator random byte generator and prevents the Coordinator from fully
+influencing the randomizer, reducing its trust assumptions.

+    Trusted dealer key generation has the severe disadvantage that it requires

+$\alpha$ and is usually generated using the $\mathsf{RedDSA.GenRandom}$ function
+as defined in the Zcash specification [#protocol-spendauthsig]_. Note that the
+choice of $\alpha$ influences the SIGHASH computation, so it is impossible to
+compute the $\mathtt{randomizer}$ based on the message (SIGHASH), as suggested
+in [#frost-rerandomized]_. This is not an issue as long as the
+$\mathtt{randomizer}$ is generated with the same security properties as
+$\mathsf{RedDSA.GenRandom}$. We ensure that by using a very similar approach;
+while the original $\mathsf{RedDSA.GenRandom}$ uses $\mathsf{H}^\circledast(T)$
+where $T$ is a random byte sequence with a certain size, in this ZIP we
+effectively use $\mathsf{H}^\circledast(T || \mathsf{signing\_commitments\_enc})$,
+i.e. we concatenate the random bytes with the encoding of the signing
+commitments. This preserves the security assumptions and also hedges against
+issues in the Coordinator random byte generator and prevents the Coordinator
+from fully influencing the randomizer, reducing its trust assumptions.

prs.author: nuttycom
prs.bodyExcerpt: Closes #1246. Updates the Sprout-to-Sapling migration parameters to reflect the faster schedule implemented in zcash/zcash#7132: - Batch interval reduced from 500 blocks to 100 blocks (triggering height \`99 mod 100\`). - Expiry delta reduced from 450 to 50 blocks. - Two-range exponent distribution:

files.patch:
From 77b7680a16c95bcd09ffbf8a299d5566a908cd40 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Kris Nuttycombe <kris@nutty.land>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:58:23 -0600
Subject: [PATCH] ZIP 308: Update migration parameters to match
 zcash/zcash#7132.

Update the Sprout-to-Sapling migration parameters to reflect the
faster schedule implemented in zcash/zcash#7132:

- Reduce the batch interval from 500 blocks to 100 blocks (triggering
  height 99 modulo 100).
- Reduce the expiry delta from 450 to 50 blocks.
- Introduce a two-range exponent distribution: 8..10 inclusive when
  the remaining amount to migrate exceeds 1 ZEC, falling back to the
  original 6..8 range otherwise.

Closes zcash/zips#1246.

prs.author: nuttycom
prs.bodyExcerpt: Closes #683. The definitions of \`tx_in_total_size\` and \`tx_out_total_size\` were ambiguous about whether the CompactSize \`tx_in_count\` and \`tx_out_count\` prefixes that precede the \`tx_in\` and \`tx_out\` arrays in the encoded transaction are included. A careful reading of the protocol specif

files.patch:
From 828ed85b2ac306fb2d5358b1650a23c079054dd5 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Kris Nuttycombe <kris@nutty.land>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:56:24 -0600
Subject: [PATCH] ZIP 317: Clarify that tx_in/out_total_size exclude
 tx_in/out_count.

The definitions of tx_in_total_size and tx_out_total_size were ambiguous
about whether the CompactSize tx_in_count and tx_out_count prefixes that
precede the tx_in and tx_out arrays in the encoded transaction are
included. A careful reading of the protocol specification implies they
are not, but the ZIP did not say so explicitly. This ambiguity led to a
bug in an initial implementation attempt.

Closes zcash/zips#683.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
---
 zips/zip-0317.rst | 7 +++++++
 1 file changed, 7 insertions(+)

diff --git a/zips/zip-0317.rst b/zips/zip-0317.rst
index 5ca8b081f..23a602e9f 100644
--- a/zips/zip-0317.rst
+++ b/zips/zip-0317.rst
@@ -163,6 +163,13 @@ Input                                         Units  Description
 :math:`\mathit{nMemoChunks}`                  number the number of memo chunks
 ============================================= ====== ====================================================================
 
+Here, :math:`\mathit{tx\_in\_total\_size}` is the sum of the sizes in bytes of the
+serialized ``tx_in`` entries, and :math:`\mathit{tx\_out\_total\_size}` is the sum of
+the sizes in bytes of the serialized ``tx_out`` entries, as defined by the Bitcoin-style
+transaction format referenced in [#protocol-txnencoding]_. These totals do not include
+the size of the ``tx_in_count`` or ``tx_out_count`` CompactSize prefixes that precede
+the ``tx_in`` and ``tx_out`` arrays in the encoded transaction.
+
 It is not a consensus requirement that fees follow this formula; however,
 wallets SHOULD create transactions that pay this fee, in order to reduce
 information leakage, unless overridden by the user.
